nodes.bodyText:
There is a call in _iter_sample to set the random seed.  It is None by default, which reseeds the generator.  This can lead to unexpected behavior when users are trying to set a random seed themselves:
import numpy as np
import pymc3 as pm

for _ in range(2):
    np.random.seed(1)
    with pm.Model():
        pm.sample(1)
    print(np.random.random()) 

this will print two different numbers.  Changing a default value can be dangerous, so wanted to open an issue along with a pull request.
nodes.title: Random seed is set unexpectedly

nodes.bodyText:
Essentially it is this problem on stackoverflow.
If attempting to fit a straight line to 2d uncertainties with MvNormal, it raises LinAlgError: Last 2 dimensions of the array must be square.
from pymc3 import  *

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

size = 200
true_intercept = 1
true_slope = 2

true_x = np.linspace(0, 1, size)
# y = a + b*x
true_regression_line = true_intercept + true_slope * true_x
# add noise

# here the errors are all the same but the real world they are usually not!
std_y, std_x = 0.1, 0.1 
y = true_regression_line + np.random.normal(scale=std_y, size=size)
x = true_x + np.random.normal(scale=std_x, size=size)

y_err = np.ones_like(y) * std_y
x_err = np.ones_like(x) * std_x

data = dict(x=x, y=y)

with Model() as model: # model specifications in PyMC3 are wrapped in a with-statement
    # Define priors
    intercept = Normal('Intercept', 0, sd=20)
    gradient = Normal('gradient', 0, sd=20)


    # Define likelihood
    likelihood = MvNormal('y', mu=intercept + gradient * x,
                        tau=1./(np.stack((y_err, x_err))**2.), observed=y)

    # start the mcmc!
    start = find_MAP() # Find starting value by optimization
    step = NUTS(scaling=start) # Instantiate MCMC sampling algorithm
    trace = sample(2000, step, start=start, progressbar=False) # draw 2000 posterior samples using NUTS sampling

It seems like this should be a common problem but I see no other questions/post about this issue.
Thanks

I'm trying to model cell X time matrix of neuronal spike times as a function of two parameters: per-cell base firing probability, and between-cell connection strength. I am basing myself largely on a paper by Rigat et al. (with a few differences), though I think the details are not important for this issue.
I have defined a custom likelihood which is a function of the full cell X time observable matrix. The likelihood of any individual cell firing at any particular time point is a function of theta, beta, and the network's firing history up to that time point. This aspect of the likelihood means (I think) that the likelihood for the full observable matrix will always involve some looping. I am implementing this looping using theano.map(), which is just a thin convenience wrapper around theano.scan(). When I execute my function using plain Theano, outside of any PyMC3 code, it works perfectly:

ntim = 10

# spikes as binary variable

# model 'parameters'
# theta: cell-specific base firing rate

# beta: cell X cell connectivity matrix

# in pymc3.distributions.distribution
theano.config.compute_test_value = 'warn'

# the rate term for one cell i and one time point t
def rate(i,t,y,theta,beta):
    # determine previous spike time of cell i
    # known as tau_it in model of Rigat
    last_time = T.flatnonzero(y[i,:t]).astype('uint16')
    # if last_time is not empty (cell i has fired at least once)
    # then use last firing time, otherwise use 0
    last_time = ifelse(
        T.gt(last_time.shape[0], 0),
        # the next line is where the error happens in pymc3 (but not in pure Theano)
        last_time[-1],
        T.constant(0, dtype='uint16')
    )

    # if t == 0 then rate term is simply theta[i]
    # otherwise it's theta[i] plus a weighted sum of all cells' firing
    # history since the last time cell i spiked
    return ifelse(
        T.eq(t, 0),
        theta[i],
        theta[i] + T.sum( beta[:,i] * \
            (T.sum(y[:,last_time:t], axis=-1) / (t-last_time)), axis=0)
    )

# symbolic variables for observed data and parameters
y_theano = T.matrix('y')
theta_theano = T.vector('theta')
beta_theano = T.matrix('beta')

# create flattened indexing grids over which rate() will loop

cgrid = cgrid.flatten().astype('uint16')
tgrid = tgrid.flatten().astype('uint16')

    sequences=[cgrid, tgrid],
    non_sequences=[y_theano, theta_theano, beta_theano]
)

# reshape back (not needed but was useful in debugging sometimes)
rateresult = T.reshape(rateresult, (ncell, ntim))

# compute log-likelihood based on rate term
logp = T.sum(y_theano * rateresult - T.log1p(T.exp(rateresult)))

# compile function
fun = theano.function(
    inputs=[y_theano, theta_theano, beta_theano],
    outputs=logp
)

# call function and print result
result = fun(y_obs, theta_true, beta_true)
print(result)
